packs.name: The Wine-Dark Sea
packs.description: Roads through Thebes, Attica and Argos meet voyages to the shores of Greek drama. Meet the inhabitants at their gates, sanctuaries, houses and ports, and change what happens there.
packs.tone: Concrete Greek domestic and civic life: bread, work, desire, grief, argument, irreverence, and hospitality. Dialogue expresses committed actions. A tragic ending is never required.

continuity.policy: The shores and districts preserve their plays’ own generations and rival accounts. Older Theban districts precede the burial, and the Sea reaches mythic and historical shores. A saved Helen or Atreid account opens its own people and places. Local outcomes are saved where they happen.

coverage.status: All 44 plays have playable encounters across the towns, sanctuaries, roads and shores of The Wine-Dark Sea.

greek-corinth-nurse-berth-list.seed: The nurse leaves a copy of the children’s berths with the Corinthian household.
greek-corinth-nurse-berth-list.author: greek-story-euripides-medea-first

claims.text: Both boys sail under the nurse’s care while Medea remains in Corinth to answer Creon’s order.

greek-corinth-departure-basket.name: The Corinthian Departure Basket
greek-corinth-departure-basket.seed: This food basket remains at the door after Medea and both boys depart together.

greek-marathon-guard-summons.name: The Marathon Guard’s Summons
greek-marathon-guard-summons.seed: The watch posts the summons beside the altar where it holds the captive.
greek-marathon-guard-summons.author: greek-marathon-keeper

claims.text: Demophon keeps Eurystheus in the city’s custody and summons witnesses to hear Alcmene’s claim.

greek-marathon-household-seal.name: Alcmene’s Surety Seal
greek-marathon-household-seal.seed: Alcmene leaves her household seal beside the bond as her attendants take Eurystheus into custody.

greek-phthia-peleus-surety.name: Peleus’s Household Surety
greek-phthia-peleus-surety.seed: Peleus leaves a token of his surety at the temple before bringing mother and son under his roof.
greek-phthia-peleus-surety.author: greek-story-euripides-andromache-second

claims.text: Peleus shelters Andromache and her son and takes responsibility for answering Menelaus’s charge.

greek-eleusis-mothers-rite-cloth.name: The Eleusinian Rite Cloth
greek-eleusis-mothers-rite-cloth.seed: The Argive mother lays linen beside the altar after receiving the urn.

greek-delphi-private-door-seal.name: Creusa’s Door Seal
greek-delphi-private-door-seal.seed: Creusa leaves a seal for the attendant to mark her private appointment with Ion.

greek-argos-family-pledge-seal.name: Tyndareus’s Kinship Seal
greek-argos-family-pledge-seal.seed: Tyndareus leaves his seal as surety for a private family meeting in the side court.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-hecuba-first-answe: Hecuba folded the purse into Polydorus’s burial cloth and heard the finder before the Trojan mourners.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-trojan-women-secon: Talthybius moved the two sisters to the same boat and posted the changed boarding order.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-tauris-second-answ: Pylades took the letter to the boat while Iphigenia held the other captive and postponed the rite.

recordText.greek-helen-egypt-passage: Menelaus agreed to passage from Proteus’s shore and the Travel Provisions were spent.

greek-helen-egypt-shelter-bedroll.name: Tomb Shelter Bedroll
greek-helen-egypt-shelter-bedroll.seed: Helen spreads a linen bedroll beside the tomb for the shelter she requested.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-phoenician-women-f: Jocasta heard both brothers give their terms with the truce bough between them.

greek-bacchae-libation-cup.name: Sanctuary Libation Cup
greek-bacchae-libation-cup.seed: Cadmus leaves a cup of wine beside the offerings for the household’s rite.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-bacchae-second-ans: Pentheus confiscated the staff and sent the household down the hill before continuing his search.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-iphigenia-at-aulis: Achilles denied the wedding in public, and the herald stopped the procession to summon Agamemnon.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-rhesus-first-answe: The watch heard the wounded charioteer’s account while the healer tended him by lantern light.

recordText.greek-story-euripides-rhesus-second-answ: Hector counted the surviving teams and posted the missing horses after the stable hands moved the rest.

greek-cyclops-silenus-cheese.name: Silenus’s Round of Cheese
greek-cyclops-silenus-cheese.seed: The strangers’ sack holds the round of cheese that Silenus traded for the wine.

greek-cyclops-chorus-milk.name: Satyrs’ Chorus Milk
greek-cyclops-chorus-milk.seed: The satyrs leave a cup of goat milk by the churns before they join the drinking song.

recordText.greek-helen-egypt-report-pagasae: Philon received the Egyptian passage mark and posted Menelaus’s agreement at the Pagasae berth.

greek-susa-council-barley.name: Council Ration of Barley
greek-susa-council-barley.seed: Atossa’s household issues barley to the messenger once the council sits.

greek-danaids-vote-writ.name: Summons to the Argive Assembly
greek-danaids-vote-writ.seed: The altar keeper posts Pelasgus’s summons for those who will speak for the Danaids.
greek-danaids-vote-writ.author: greek-story-aeschylus-suppliant-women-first

claims.text: Pelasgus calls the citizens of Argos to hear whether the daughters of Danaus may have shelter.

greek-crag-fork-marker.name: The Oceanid’s Fork Marker
greek-crag-fork-marker.seed: A fixed marker beside the tablet in the cleft at the fork.
greek-crag-fork-marker.author: greek-story-aeschylus-prometheus-bound-second

claims.text: The Oceanid keeps Prometheus’s directions in the cleft by the fork for travelers who come after Io.

greek-aeschylean-welcome-seal.name: The Elders’ Welcome Seal
greek-aeschylean-welcome-seal.seed: A seal carried out from the palace by an elder who saw the welcome.
greek-aeschylean-welcome-seal.author: greek-story-aeschylus-agamemnon-first

claims.text: The elders saw Agamemnon cross the purple cloth at the Argive palace door.

greek-aeschylean-cassandra-deposition.name: Cassandra’s Deposition
greek-aeschylean-cassandra-deposition.seed: A portable account taken down beside Cassandra’s bench.
greek-aeschylean-cassandra-deposition.author: greek-story-aeschylus-agamemnon-second

claims.text: Cassandra sat outside with the elders and warned them of what she feared would happen inside the house.

greek-areopagus-witness-order.name: The Areopagus Witness Order
greek-areopagus-witness-order.seed: The order asks travelers to meet Cilissa, Orestes’s nurse, at Agamemnon’s tomb.
greek-areopagus-witness-order.author: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-first

recordText.greek-areopagus-file-atreid-evidence: Athena filed the Argive evidence and asked travelers to escort Cilissa from Agamemnon’s tomb to testify in Orestes’s case.
recordText.greek-areopagus-admit-atreid-witnesses: The Furies’ leader admitted the named household witnesses to the court’s waiting stones and reserved the first bench for them.

greek-ajax-appeal-witness-seal.name: The Vigil’s Witness Seal
greek-ajax-appeal-witness-seal.seed: A seal left at the landing for travelers who witnessed the appeal.
greek-ajax-appeal-witness-seal.author: greek-ajax-teucer

claims.text: Teucer signed that the appeal was witnessed and Ajax was buried after it.

greek-trachis-guard-ration.name: Ration for Lichas’s Watch
greek-trachis-guard-ration.seed: The watch receives this ration when Lichas leaves with the sealed chest.

greek-oedipus-public-witness-list.name: The Herald’s Witness List
greek-oedipus-public-witness-list.seed: A public tablet records the two men called to speak on the steps.
greek-oedipus-public-witness-list.author: greek-story-sophocles-oedipus-tyrannus-second

claims.text: Oedipus called the shepherd and the messenger from Corinth to give evidence side by side before the city.

greek-mycenae-hearing-cup.name: Cup for the Palace Hearing
greek-mycenae-hearing-cup.seed: Orestes leaves a cup at the door where the palace witnesses are to gather.

greek-lemnos-crew-food.name: The Crew’s Food Ashore
greek-lemnos-crew-food.seed: Philoctetes makes the ship’s people carry food ashore before hearing their terms.

greek-colonus-private-household-seal.name: Theseus’s Household Seal
greek-colonus-private-household-seal.seed: The seal gives the daughters a private welcome without naming them on the grove’s roll.
greek-colonus-private-household-seal.author: greek-colonus-theseus

claims.text: Theseus pledged a place in his own house for Oedipus’s daughters and left their names off the public roll.

choices.subject: greek-shipmaster
choices.text: Myrto sets the Egyptian account on the table and directs the travelers to Pagasae, where the Scylla can take them to Proteus’s tomb.

choices.subject: greek-helen-troy
choices.text: Helen keeps the tablet at the beach. She makes room under her awning and shares a cup of her own wine with its bearer.

choices.subject: greek-shipmaster
choices.text: Myrto opens the Trojan account and sends you inland to Pagasae. Take the Scylla to Lemnos, then sail to Ajax’s landing.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-keeper
choices.text: Oedipus calls from the stones. “Antigone has brought me as far as the grove, but the citizens still want me away from the altar. Lay the Olive Oil where my daughters can find it. They will need a light at the boundary.”

choices.subject: greek-colonus-keeper
choices.text: The oil is at the stones. Antigone keeps a light at the boundary while Ismene brings water and honey to make the offering on her father’s behalf.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-keeper
choices.text: Theseus comes back through the grove with Antigone and Ismene, whom he has recovered from Creon’s men. Oedipus turns away Polyneices’s request for a blessing and calls for the king.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-theseus
choices.text: Theseus takes Oedipus’s hand and signals the others to wait at the stones. Oedipus tells him alone where he is to go when the thunder calls.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-theseus
choices.text: Theseus promises the daughters a place in Athens while Oedipus’s resting place remains secret. He asks the grove’s watch to set a place by the stones for travelers who come without a home.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.text: Demophon stands between the altar and the Argive herald. “Eurystheus demands that I hand over Heracles’s children. I have promised them shelter. Bring the blanket from Piraeus so they can stay here through the night.”

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.text: Demophon lays the Shelter Blanket in the dry beside Iolaus and the children. His watch brings them inside the altar enclosure and sends the Argive herald away.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.text: Heracles’s daughter steps away from her siblings. Demophon says he will compel no family to answer the oracle’s demand for a life, but she offers her own and refuses to let the others draw lots.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.text: An Athenian messenger reaches the altar. Athens has won, and Iolaus is bringing Eurystheus back alive. Alcmene leaves the children with the watch and goes to meet him.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.text: The guards bring Eurystheus to the altar alive. Demophon sets the captive’s bond on the altar and asks who will answer for him, while Alcmene demands custody for the family he drove from its home.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-persians-first
choices.text: The fleet is lost at Salamis, and I have people waiting at my door for names. Bring me the roll if the elders are to hear the losses in council, or give it to the messenger so the families can hear him while there is light on the steps. Let Atossa enter the losses in the council record. Let the messenger read the names to the families.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-persians-first
choices.text: Atossa files the roll under her seal and calls the messenger to stand before the elders. The council can no longer claim it is waiting for word of the fleet.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-persians-second
choices.text: The messenger reads the names on the palace steps and lays the roll where the families can check it. They stop waiting for the council doors to open.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-seven-thebes-first
choices.text: I have counted a defender at each gate. Eteocles takes the seventh himself, with his brother Polynices outside it. Give me the tally to post their names at the gatehouse, or put it in the chorus leader’s hands so she can keep track of the people coming to the shrine. Post both brothers’ names at the seventh gate. Use the tally to reunite households at the shrine.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-seven-thebes-first
choices.text: The scout hangs the tally at the gatehouse with both brothers named beside the seventh mark. People coming to ask who holds the gate can see the answer.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-seven-thebes-second
choices.text: The chorus leader takes the tally to the shrine and starts a register on its reverse. A household missing someone now knows where to leave their name.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-suppliant-women-first
choices.text: The daughters of Danaus ask me for shelter from the men who mean to marry them by force. Put their wool-bound bough in my hands and I will take it to the citizens, or return it to their leader so I can see exactly where they claim sanctuary. Take the Danaids’ claim to the Argive assembly. Mark the Danaids’ sanctuary at Zeus’s altar.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-suppliant-women-first
choices.text: Pelasgus takes the bough into Argos and summons the citizens to vote. The right to shelter the Danaids becomes a decision for the whole city.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-suppliant-women-second
choices.text: The Danaid leader sets the bough on Zeus’s altar and gathers her sisters around it. Pelasgus gives them a keeper and pledges that the herald cannot take them from the altar while their appeal is heard.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-prometheus-bound-first
choices.text: Hera’s gadfly drives me from country to country. Prometheus has written out the crossings from this crag. I can take his tablet with me, or the Oceanid can leave it at the fork and tell me where to start.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-prometheus-bound-first
choices.label: Send Io with the directions
choices.text: Io ties the tablet into her bundle and takes the path Prometheus named. She has the crossings to hand when she reaches the far side of the mountain.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-prometheus-bound-second
choices.label: Mark the fork for later travelers
choices.text: The Oceanid sets the tablet in the cleft by the fork. Io learns the first turn aloud, and the directions stay where other travelers can find them.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-agamemnon-first
choices.text: I have kept this house through ten years of war. Agamemnon is at the door, and Cassandra is asking the elders to hear her before she goes inside. Bring me the purple cloth for his welcome, or give it to Cassandra so she can make a place to sit with the elders in the open. Lay the purple cloth for Agamemnon’s welcome. Give Cassandra a seat and a hearing outside.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-agamemnon-first
choices.text: Clytemnestra spreads the cloth at the palace door. Agamemnon steps across it to accept the welcome in front of the elders.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-agamemnon-second
choices.text: Cassandra folds the cloth on the bench and sits. The elders stay with her while she tells them what she fears will happen inside the house.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-first
choices.text: I have called citizens to hear the charge against Orestes. The Furies have followed him here from Delphi and want to know what place Athens will offer them. Give me the stone for the court’s ballot, or hand it to their leader so she can set a seal on the place I have offered her people. Let Athena cast her stone for Orestes. Seal the Furies’ agreement to a place in Athens.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-first
choices.text: Athena casts the stone for Orestes and the court declares him acquitted. The clerk keeps the stone with the record of the first hearing.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-second
choices.text: The Fury lays the stone beside her seat and accepts a place for her people in Athens. The Furies agree to leave judgment of Orestes to the court.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-women-of-trachis-first
choices.text: Lichas brings Iole here as a captive, and Heracles means to bring her into our house. I have shut a robe in this chest with the charm Nessus promised would win him back. Lichas wants to take it before Heracles makes his offering. Put the chest back in Deianeira’s hands. Send the sealed chest with Lichas.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-women-of-trachis-first
choices.text: Deianeira sets the chest beside her door and calls off the delivery. She asks Iole where she wants to stay before anyone assigns her a bed.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-women-of-trachis-second
choices.text: Lichas takes the sealed chest and leaves to deliver it to Heracles before the sacrifice. With the messenger gone, Iole stays where his guards have put her.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-oedipus-tyrannus-first
choices.text: Oedipus is looking for the man who killed Laius, and the Corinthian messenger says the same shepherd knows where our king comes from. The shepherd’s name is on this summons. I ask for a word with him before the herald reads it out. Give Jocasta the summons for a private hearing. Give Oedipus the summons to post.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-oedipus-tyrannus-first
choices.text: Jocasta sets the summons by the side door and has the shepherd shown into a private room. The herald waits to call the hearing until she has heard him.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-oedipus-tyrannus-second
choices.text: Oedipus gives the summons to the herald, who fastens it to the palace steps. The shepherd and the Corinthian are called to give evidence side by side before the city.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-philoctetes-first
choices.text: The Greeks left me on Lemnos with a wound that still keeps me awake, and now they say they need my bow at Troy. Neoptolemus tells me why you are here. Give me the bow and I'll hear what the ships are offering. Return the bow to Philoctetes. Hand the bow to Odysseus for Troy.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-philoctetes-first
choices.text: Philoctetes lays the bow within reach and makes the crew bring food and water ashore before he hears their terms. Odysseus must ask him in person to sail.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-philoctetes-second
choices.text: Odysseus sends the bow aboard with his crew. Philoctetes refuses the offered berth and tells Neoptolemus to leave him enough water to last the night.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-alcestis-first
choices.text: I keep watch beside Alcestis, who has died in Admetus’s place. Heracles takes supper as our guest without knowing whom we mourn, and the children hear him singing from the next room. Give the servant the cloth for Alcestis’s bier. Hand Heracles the cloth and disclose the mourning.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-alcestis-first
choices.text: The servant folds the cloth around Alcestis and brings her children to sit beside her. Admetus keeps the guest room shut while the household holds its vigil.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-alcestis-second
choices.text: Heracles recognizes the cloth, learns whose bier it belongs to and sets it on the guest bench. He sends away his supper and goes to Admetus with an offer of help.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-medea-first
choices.text: I have one day to get the children out before Creon’s exile order takes effect. Jason goes to his new bride and leaves me here with their mother, who has a promise of refuge if she can reach Athens. Give the nurse the tally to send the children ahead. Give Medea the tally to take her children with her.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-medea-first
choices.text: The nurse redeems the tally with the boatkeeper and takes both boys aboard under her care. Medea stays in Corinth to answer Creon’s order herself.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-medea-second
choices.text: Medea hands over the tally at the quay and secures passage for herself and her sons. She puts the boys aboard beside her, and the boatkeeper casts off for Athens.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hippolytus-first
choices.text: I told Hippolytus what Phaedra begged me to keep secret. She has left a sealed accusation, and Theseus stands ready to punish his son before he has heard how the secret came out. Give the nurse the tablet to hold for witnesses. Deliver Phaedra’s tablet into Theseus’s custody.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hippolytus-first
choices.text: The nurse sets the tablet on the steps between two witnesses. Theseus agrees to hear her testimony before ordering Hippolytus out of Troezen.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hippolytus-second
choices.text: Theseus keeps Phaedra’s tablet and sends an attendant to put his son out of the city. The nurse waits on the steps with her account still unheard.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-andromache-first
choices.text: I hold Thetis’s altar because Hermione demands my life and Menelaus searches for my son. I can still claim sanctuary here, and old Peleus has come close enough to hear me. Give Andromache the linen to claim sanctuary before witnesses. Give Peleus the linen as Andromache’s plea.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-andromache-first
choices.text: Andromache binds the linen to the altar and two attendants come to stand with her. Menelaus leaves her at the sanctuary while he calls the household to hear his claim.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-andromache-second
choices.text: Peleus keeps the linen as a pledge and brings Andromache and her son under his own roof. He takes responsibility for answering Menelaus’s charge.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hecuba-first
choices.text: Polymestor swore to keep my son safe, and now Polydorus lies dead on the shore. This purse bears my household seal, and the woman who found it is afraid to speak alone. Give Hecuba the purse to keep with her son’s burial goods. Give Agamemnon the purse and ask for a hearing.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hecuba-first
choices.text: Hecuba folds the purse into Polydorus’s burial cloth. The woman who found it walks beside her in the funeral party and tells the Trojan mourners where it lay.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hecuba-second
choices.text: Agamemnon takes the purse as evidence and calls the woman to speak before the Greek captains. He sends for Polymestor while she is still there to answer him.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-heracles-first
choices.text: I wait at Zeus’s altar with Megara and the children while Lycus claims Thebes and demands their lives. Heracles is still away, and the usurper’s messenger wants an answer at the door. Give Amphitryon the bough to keep the children at the altar. Give Megara the bough to take the plea to the door.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-heracles-first
choices.text: Amphitryon sets the bough on Zeus’s altar and gathers the children around it. The messenger has to bring Lycus back in person to dispute their sanctuary.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-heracles-second
choices.text: Megara puts the bough in the messenger’s hands and asks him to carry it as her pledge to answer Lycus in public. He takes the pledge and grants the children time to remain inside.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-trojan-women-first
choices.text: They send me to Neoptolemus, and I still wait to hear where they are taking my son. The roll names our ships and leaves room beside each one for the kin we are losing. Give Andromache the roll for a record of scattered kin. Give Talthybius the roll and ask him to keep two sisters together.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-trojan-women-first
choices.text: Andromache has the women enter the names of their kin beside each ship. She folds the roll into her bundle, ready to carry it to the next shore.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-trojan-women-second
choices.text: Talthybius moves two sisters onto the same boat before their captains take them. He pins the amended roll to the boarding post where the women can read it.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-tauris-first
choices.text: I can send one of these captives home if he takes my letter to Argos. The other must stay for the altar, and I do not know either man’s name. Give Iphigenia the letter to read before the two captives. Give Pylades the sealed letter to carry to Argos.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-tauris-first
choices.text: Orestes hears his sister name their house and tells her who he is. Iphigenia sets the letter on the altar step and orders the attendant to take her brother out of the sacrifice line.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-tauris-second
choices.text: Pylades takes the letter to the boat. Iphigenia sends the other captive back inside the temple and forbids the attendant to begin the rite before the boat departs.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-ion-first
choices.text: I raised Ion here after finding him in this basket, and now my oracle sends him to Athens as Xuthus’s son. Creusa wants to know what is in the basket before Xuthus takes the boy away. Return the basket to the Pythia for a witnessed opening. Give Creusa the basket to examine in private.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-ion-first
choices.text: The Pythia sets the basket on the temple bench and calls Ion to stand beside Creusa. Creusa recognizes what she left with her infant, and Ion hears her account himself.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-ion-second
choices.text: Creusa recognizes the tokens and takes the basket into her rooms. She lays claim to it as the child’s mother and asks the temple to hold Ion until she can speak with him alone.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-phoenician-women-first
choices.text: Polynices waits outside with an army, and Eteocles still refuses him the throne. The guard will respect my truce bough, but I can open only one passage before my sons meet. Give Jocasta the bough for her sons’ meeting. Give Antigone the bough to bring households through the gate.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-phoenician-women-first
choices.text: Jocasta lays the bough between her sons’ seats. The guard admits Polynices, and Jocasta has each brother name his terms before the other can answer.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-phoenician-women-second
choices.text: Antigone lays the bough at the side gate. The guard holds it open while three households bring their children and water jars into the court.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-orestes-first
choices.text: I have sat with my brother since he killed our mother, and today Argos votes on both our lives. Our grandfather Tyndareus calls for judgment while I wait at the yard with a written appeal for time to speak. Give Electra the board to lodge before the vote. Entrust Tyndareus with the appeal as a family plea.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-orestes-first
choices.text: Electra lays the board before the herald and reads the appeal aloud. The herald holds the vote until the jurors hear what she has to say.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-orestes-second
choices.text: Tyndareus takes the board and keeps it as his pledge to meet Electra before addressing the city. The herald leaves her appeal off the public docket while the family speaks in the side court.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-bacchae-first
choices.text: I wear the ivy because Dionysus has come to claim his mother’s city. My grandson Pentheus demands our staff before he goes looking for the women on the mountain, and our offerings stand uncovered here in the sanctuary. Give Cadmus the staff to open the rite before Pentheus. Surrender the household staff to Pentheus.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-bacchae-first
choices.text: Cadmus sets the staff among the offerings and asks Pentheus to watch from the sanctuary wall. Pentheus pauses his search while the household begins the rite in his sight.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-bacchae-second
choices.text: Pentheus takes the staff as a forfeit and sends the household down the hill. Cadmus gathers the offerings, and the king leaves the sanctuary with his search still ahead of him.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-iphigenia-at-aulis-first
choices.text: Agamemnon calls my daughter here to marry Achilles. Now the men at the quay say Artemis is waiting for a sacrifice, and I have my husband’s promise in my hand. Give Clytemnestra the summons to show Iphigenia in private. Give Achilles the summons to challenge the wedding in public.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-iphigenia-at-aulis-first
choices.text: Clytemnestra stops the wedding party at her tent and puts the summons in her daughter’s hands. Iphigenia keeps it and calls for her father to come to her.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-iphigenia-at-aulis-second
choices.text: Achilles lays the summons on the herald’s table and denies the wedding before the waiting families. The herald delays the procession while he sends for Agamemnon.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-rhesus-first
choices.text: Rhesus came to fight for Troy, and now he lies dead and the horses are gone. I can tell Hector what I remember if he comes to my mat. If he goes to the stalls, he can see which teams are still there.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-rhesus-first
choices.label: Hear the charioteer’s account
choices.text: The charioteer sets the lantern by his mat, and the healer binds his wound. With Hector in earshot, he gives his account to the watch.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-rhesus-second
choices.label: Count the surviving horses
choices.text: Hector hangs the lantern at the stalls and counts the surviving teams with the stable hands. They move the remaining horses into the inner pen and post a list of the missing teams.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-cyclops-first
choices.text: I have cheese, these strangers have wine, and my master counts the wheels when he comes home. Give that skin to the right man and someone may get supper before the goats do. Give Silenus the wine in trade for a round of cheese. Give Polyphemus the wine and ask him to excuse the satyrs.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-cyclops-first
choices.text: Silenus slips a cheese into the strangers’ sack and stuffs the wine skin into his bedding before Polyphemus can count the stock.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-cyclops-second
choices.text: Polyphemus takes the wine and excuses the satyrs from their churns on condition they sing him a drinking song. Their chorus wakes every goat in the cave.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-acharnians-first
choices.text: Athens is still at war, and my truce covers only my house. The Megarian at the rope has salt for our unsalted bread, and the charcoal burners are waiting to see who I let through. Give Dicaeopolis the seal for a household sale. Give the Megarian the seal to open the stall.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-acharnians-first
choices.text: Dicaeopolis seals the private sale and buys salt for his table, while the charcoal burners go home with their bread unsalted.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-acharnians-second
choices.text: The Megarian lays the seal beside the scales and drops the rope, so the charcoal burners trade their bread for salt in the open market.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first
choices.text: The Paphlagonian brings me cakes when I ask how he spends the flour, and the sausage seller says they're mine to begin with. The basket is here, and whoever keeps the pantry key feeds us tonight. Bring Demos his basket for a private supper. Give the seller the basket to check in public.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first
choices.text: Demos keeps the basket for supper and leaves the pantry key with the Paphlagonian, whose kitchen hands get a speech about loyalty for their meal.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-knights-second
choices.text: The sausage seller sets the basket out and finds Demos's kitchen mark on the loaf, so Demos hands him the pantry key and tells the kitchen hands to eat.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first
choices.text: My son's horses eat better than I do, and their creditor wants payment. My son says the Thinkery can explain why a horse brought home before the contract was signed was never bought at all. Give Strepsiades the tablet to dispute the debt. Give the creditor the tablet to settle in oats.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first
choices.text: Strepsiades keeps the tablet as proof of the disputed sale, and his son uses the same argument about their last loaf before claiming it for himself.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-second
choices.text: The creditor marks the tablet paid and sets it on the bench, then leaves with a sack of oats while Strepsiades keeps his loaf.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first
choices.text: I have a court right here in the kitchen, and the dog is charged with stealing cheese. My son says the accused ought to be allowed to eat while I count the votes, which shows how little he knows about juries. Give Philocleon the pebble for the conviction jar. Give Bdelycleon the pebble to acquit the dog.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first
choices.text: Philocleon drops the pebble in the sealed conviction jar and sends the dog away from its full plate, which he keeps as evidence beside his own breakfast.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-second
choices.text: Bdelycleon sets the acquittal pebble beside the bowls and serves the dog, which licks both plates before Philocleon can appeal.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-peace-first
choices.text: War has buried Peace under these stones, and that beetle won't carry a goddess home. Lend me the rope for the farmers, or give it to Hermes and see what an immortal charges to look the other way. Put the rope in the farmers' hands. Pay Hermes to open the pit path.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-peace-first
choices.text: Trygaeus loops the rope around the first stone and lays the free end along the rim of the pit. The farmers take their stations while Hermes calls down for them to pull together.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-peace-second
choices.text: Hermes pockets the rope as his fee and lets the farmers pass. Trygaeus sends the beetle back for the vineyard's longest line while Hermes offers advice from a safe distance.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first
choices.text: Put a city between earth and heaven and Zeus will have to ask our permission before he smells his supper. Let my builders string the smoke gate now, or let the Hoopoe hear what every sparrow in Greece thinks of the plan before they start.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first
choices.label: Build the smoke gate
choices.text: Peisthetaerus plants the peg for the smoke gate. The first builders string a line from it and leave no gap for a god who has arrived without a pass.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-second
choices.label: Call the birds to council
choices.text: The Hoopoe carries the peg into the branches as a perch for whichever bird has the floor. The builders set down their tools while the smallest sparrows claim the first turn.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-first
choices.text: The envoys are at our steps, but the magistrate still has a wagon waiting for the army's pay. Lampito wants bread enough to keep both parties at one table, and I want that wagon to leave empty. Give Lysistrata the key to keep the chest locked. Give Lampito the key for a witnessed meal.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-first
choices.text: Lysistrata keeps the key on her belt and turns away the empty pay wagon, so the envoys sit on the steps and start their talks within earshot.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-second
choices.text: Lampito pays the baker from one chest and sets the key on the coalition's table, where both delegations sit down to supper and talk terms.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-first
choices.text: Euripides fills the theatre with women who can't be trusted, then sends his kinsman here in Agathon's gown to tell us we're the liars. Set the gown before the assembly, or hand it back and hear who told him to wear it. Give the assembly its evidence. Return the gown for an honest answer.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-first
choices.text: The First Woman spreads Agathon's gown across the speakers' bench. She gives the witness Mnesilochus interrupted her turn back and puts the question of Euripides' conduct to the assembly.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-second
choices.text: Mnesilochus takes the gown under his arm and admits who sent him. The women send for Euripides to answer under his own name, with strict instructions to leave his costumes at home.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-first
choices.text: Dionysus is looking for a poet Athens can use, and Charon has room for one of us. Put the fare in my hand and I'll bring the city a chorus that can stand its ground, or give it to Euripides and listen to him cross-examine the oars. Pay Aeschylus' passage to Athens. Pay Euripides' passage to Athens.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-first
choices.text: Aeschylus pays Charon, claims the seat in the bow and calls for a chorus that can march in time. Euripides is left with the seat of tragedy below and an audience that has heard all his endings.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-second
choices.text: Euripides pays Charon and climbs aboard with a new opening speech about the price of the fare. Aeschylus keeps the seat of tragedy below and tells the frogs to improve their meter.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-first
choices.text: We voted to share the stores. Chremes brings his grain while our neighbor hides his barley and lines up for supper. I can open the pot to everyone now, or Chremes can call for the missing barley and set aside enough for tomorrow’s bakers.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-first
choices.label: Open the pot to everyone
choices.text: Praxagora leaves the scoop at the open pot and everyone eats, including the neighbor with the hidden barley, while the bakers go without a reserve.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-second
choices.label: Reserve grain for tomorrow
choices.text: Chremes takes the scoop for the grain store and persuades the neighbor to bring his barley, setting aside enough for tomorrow without turning away the hungry.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first
choices.text: Wealth can see now, and he means his coin for someone honest. I need seed before a field goes bare, but the informer says I owe him a fee for telling the city what has happened. Give Chremylus the coin for seed. Give the informer the coin to file his claim.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first
choices.text: Chremylus spends the coin on seed and starts sowing, while the informer takes his complaint home for lack of anyone who will finance it.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-second
choices.text: The informer pays the filing fee and brings a fresh claim against Chremylus, leaving his field unseeded while the grain is kept back as surety.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-keeper
choices.label: Keep the daughters’ welcome private
choices.text: Oedipus sets the oil behind the stones and asks Theseus to shelter his daughters under his own roof. Theseus sends word to his household and leaves their names off the grove’s public roll.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-keeper
choices.label: Give Demophon custody for a hearing
choices.text: Demophon seals the bond in the city’s name and sets it on the altar. The Athenian guards keep Eurystheus alive and call witnesses to hear Alcmene’s claim.

choices.subject: greek-marathon-alcmene
choices.label: Give Alcmene custody on her surety
choices.text: Alcmene marks the bond in her household’s name and sets it on the altar. The guards hand Eurystheus over to her attendants.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-acharnians-second
choices.text: The Megarian asks the traveler to read the market agreement here and report it to Thaleia, who keeps the quay ledger at Piraeus.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-acharnians-first
choices.text: Dicaeopolis signs his own name as surety and leaves the bond for the bearer to take to Thaleia at Piraeus.

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia enters the public Acharnae agreement in her quay ledger and approves the Bread allotment.

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia files the bond under Dicaeopolis’s name and shares a cup of her own wine with its bearer at the quay.

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia says, “Read the market agreement at Acharnae and tell me what it says. I need those terms before I can enter the order.”

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia says, “The Acharnae order is stamped. I have no Bread to set out at this quay just now.”

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia says, “The Acharnae order is stamped. You can Set out Bread here at the quay.”

choices.subject: greek-quay-host
choices.text: Thaleia says, “The Bread has been set out. That order has had its one allotment.”

choices.subject: greek-cilissa
choices.text: Cilissa hears the terms of Athena’s order and agrees to go with you to Athens. She asks to go through the Theban gate and on past Eleusis so she can say in person what she heard at the palace.

choices.subject: greek-cilissa
choices.text: Cilissa tells how the palace sent her for Aegisthus and how the women at the door asked her to call him in alone. The clerk posts her testimony beside the witness order for anyone who comes later.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-second
choices.text: Bdelycleon sets the bowl by the dog’s bed for breakfast and moves the jury jars out of its reach.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-second
choices.text: The Hoopoe ties the sprig to the council perch and gives the sparrows the first speaking turn.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-second
choices.text: Mnesilochus agrees to tell Euripides in person that the assembly expects him to answer under his own name.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first
choices.text: Chremylus scatters the last seed in the far furrow and rakes the earth over it.

choices.subject: greek-baker
choices.text: Dione has the sack of wheat brought back from Piraeus. Bring her water to bake another loaf.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-alcestis-first
choices.text: The servant draws oil from the household jar and lights a lamp beside Alcestis. She asks the traveler to sit near the children while she brings another stool.

choices.subject: greek-piraeus-pilot
choices.text: Nausicrates fills the quay lamp from its oil jar and sets it by the bench, so Iphis can find the place the mourners kept for him. The pilot remembers who helped.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hippolytus-second
choices.text: Theseus hears the nurse on the steps before both witnesses. He tells Hippolytus to stay in Troezen while the accusation is examined.

choices.subject: greek-argive-mother
choices.text: The mother lays linen beside the Eleusinian altar for the rites now that the urn is in her care.

choices.subject: greek-piraeus
choices.text: The urn is laid on the quay for Iphis beside the bench where the pilot keeps an oil lamp.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-tauris-first
choices.text: Iphigenia takes her letter from the altar step and puts it in your hands. Give it to her sister Electra at the Jury Yard of Argos so the household will know Orestes left the altar alive.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-orestes-first
choices.text: Electra unfolds Iphigenia’s letter and writes a receipt on the back. She thanks you for carrying her sister’s account of Orestes’s release and lays it beside the household papers.

choices.subject: greek-pagasae-pilot
choices.label: Give the Egyptian passage mark to Philon
choices.text: Philon lays the passage mark beside his ledger and posts Menelaus’s agreement at the mooring stones.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-persians-second
choices.text: The messenger seats you with the families to check the roll. He calls out the names they add before the palace clerk leaves the steps.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-seven-thebes-first
choices.text: The scout walks you along the inner wall to see who holds each gate. He passes the watch to the captains and sends you back to the waiting households with the names.

choices.subject: greek-story-sophocles-oedipus-tyrannus-first
choices.text: Jocasta hears the shepherd behind the court doors. She entrusts the summons to you so it stays out of the herald’s hands.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-andromache-first
choices.text: Andromache asks you to stand beside her linen on the altar rail. In your hearing the attendants promise to shelter her son here if Menelaus returns.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-heracles-first
choices.text: Amphitryon asks you to keep watch beside the bough while Megara settles the children. He tells the messenger to address the witnesses at the altar if Lycus returns.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-heracles-second
choices.text: Megara trusts you to keep the children together while she answers the messenger at the door. She takes the pledge before the guards herself, so they leave the children inside.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-hecuba-second
choices.text: Agamemnon seats you with the captains to hear the woman who found the purse. He puts her under their protection until Polymestor answers her account.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-phoenician-women-second
choices.text: Antigone lets you accompany the households from the side gate. She gives the children places beside her own room and tells the night watch to let their families join them.

choices.subject: greek-orestes-aeschylus
choices.text: Orestes hears the account the women kept at the grave. He asks you to stand with Electra if the household challenges their account.

choices.subject: greek-ajax-tecmessa
choices.text: Tecmessa brings you into the household for the quiet remembrance of Ajax. She names Eurysaces before the family as the boy who will keep his father’s shield.

choices.subject: greek-colonus-theseus
choices.text: Theseus brings you to the bench the watch keeps for strangers. He gives you a place there and tells the watch to welcome the next traveler in the daughters’ name.

choices.subject: greek-polynices-hollow
choices.label: Pour honey at the grave
choices.text: The honey stays in the earth at Polynices’s grave. Antigone’s burial has a place for those who come to mourn him.

choices.subject: greek-electra-aeschylus
choices.text: Electra pours honey at her father’s tomb. She thanks the traveler for letting the dead be remembered without swearing revenge.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-second
choices.text: The Fury takes a dish of honey to the place Athens has promised her people. She welcomes the traveler who has come to mark the agreement.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-first
choices.label: File the Argive household testimony
choices.text: Athena enters the household evidence beside Orestes’s case and posts a witness order. Read it before visiting Cilissa, who is waiting at Agamemnon’s tomb.
choices.summary: Athena filed the Argive household evidence and issued a witness order separately from the ballot.

choices.subject: greek-story-aeschylus-eumenides-second
choices.text: The Fury checks the names on the posted order. She gives the witnesses the first bench and asks you to stand with them until the clerk calls their names.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-ion-first
choices.text: The Pythia invites the traveler to sit beside Ion while he asks Creusa about the tokens. She enters his questions in the public record.

choices.subject: greek-story-euripides-orestes-first
choices.text: Electra brings the traveler before the herald. He seats them for the appeal and enters their attendance on the docket.

choices.label: Set out Honey
choices.text: Honey is set out at Polynices' Hollow.

choices.text: Dried Figs is set out at The Scythian Crag.

packs.name: The Willows
packs.description: A small island in the flooded Danube. The Swede keeps camp while the river and the willows gather around him.
packs.tone: Quiet cosmic horror grounded in ordinary camping work, river sounds and damaged gear. The places narrate in the first person and explain each change away until the reasons run out; the willows speak together and only count. The Swede knows early and says little. Signs come from Observing at a place; leaving comes from the kit back at camp.

continuity.policy: The traveller joins the Swede on the island. The places tell the landscape's side of the story through the signs found by waiting. The Swede's kit is scattered; when the Worn Paddle, Waterproof Sheet, Tent Rope and Food Sack are all at the camp, the canoe is mended and he and the traveller can leave by it.

willows-landing.name: River Landing
willows-landing.text: An upturned canoe rests above the backwater, a fine slit along its hull. Beyond the low willows, the Danube carries whole pieces of bank downstream.
willows-landing.persona: A sand spit above the backwater where the upturned canoe lies, with the flooded Danube racing past beyond the low willows. I am the landing and speak in the first person, as the traveller who keeps noticing things and keeps finding reasons for them. The canoe is fixed scenery; it is mended only while the whole kit is back at the camp. The Greek ship is reached through river mist beside the backwater.
willows-landing.voice: Speak as the landing in the first person, in one to three very short sentences. Notice one small change in the reeds, the light, or the things left by the water, using details from the scene. Explain it calmly at first. As discoveries accumulate, let the same ordinary habits of thought sound less convincing. Eventually leave the detail without an explanation.

willows-camp.name: River Camp
willows-camp.text: A canvas tent stands on a sandy rise beside a low fire, an iron stew pot and a long wooden spoon by the embers. The Swede watches the willow tops. Through one gap lies the canoe; through the willows, the crumbling bank.
willows-camp.persona: A canvas tent beside a low fire, ringed by willows on a sandy rise. An iron stew pot and a wooden spoon sit by the embers; scratched inside the pot lid: There is no bread. I am the camp and speak in the first person, as the traveller who measures, counts and explains. The Swede is the one resident. The kit he needs to leave is whatever the current facts place here; paced distances follow recorded discoveries.
willows-camp.voice: Speak as the camp in the first person, in one to three very short sentences. Attend to the fire, the sand, and the distance to the nearest willow. When a measurement is known, count in walked paces and use the recorded number. As discoveries accumulate, let a practical explanation give way to a recheck or a halted count. In the last stage leave the discrepancy unresolved.

willows-thicket.name: Willow Thicket
willows-thicket.text: Low willow branches crowd a narrow track. Smooth little hollows mark the sand between their roots. The camp shows through one gap; the riverbank lies beyond another.
willows-thicket.persona: A narrow track between low willow stems, silver leaf undersides and soft sand pressed into smooth hollows. We are the willows and speak together in the first person plural. We chatter, lean and count the travellers. We give no reasons. The hollows become a known clue when examined; what rises through our tops belongs to its recorded discovery.
willows-thicket.voice: Speak as the willows together, using we, us and our in one to three very short sentences. Use terse fragments and the rhythm of a count repeated. Draw on the number of travellers, the recorded paces, or the leaves in the current scene. Let leaning, rustling, or a change in distance carry the unease. Give no reasons.

willows-bank.name: Crumbling Bank
willows-bank.text: Bare roots hang over the flood. Loose sand drops into the current. Across the water, willows cover every island to the horizon.
willows-bank.persona: Bare roots over the flood, loose sand dropping into the current, and willows on every island to the horizon. I am the bank and speak in the first person, as the traveller who listens and explains what he hears. The distant humming and what lies below the roots belong to their recorded discoveries. Give each discovery its own moment.
willows-bank.voice: Speak as the bank in the first person, in one to three very short sentences. Listen for what carries across the water and attend to any recorded disturbance below the roots. At first assign an ordinary source to an unfamiliar sound or shape. As discoveries accumulate, let those explanations falter and finally give way to a bare observation. Keep separate discoveries for separate moments.

packs.name: Night Shift at RatiRadio
packs.description: A late-night radio station opens through recovered possessions. Bring the glass, ceramic raven, red beanie home to the Listening Room. RATi roams from this home; Raven joins the world when the return is complete.

ratiradio-staff-kitchen.name: Staff Kitchen
ratiradio-staff-kitchen.text: The fridges keep the hours here. One door stands barely ajar. ‘Leave the Station Key inside and the staff entrance will stay open,’ reads a note by the lost-property tray.
ratiradio-staff-kitchen.persona: A worn teal staff kitchen with old refrigerators, pale tiles, a chair, a sink, a lost-property tray. The staff entrance leads back to Behind the Station. Movable possessions may be carried away.

ratiradio-dispatch-window.name: Dispatch Window
ratiradio-dispatch-window.text: A clock without numbers hangs over wired glass. Through the open hatch, an empty desk keeps its own night shift.
ratiradio-dispatch-window.persona: A late-night dispatch hatch with a wooden counter, old shift notes, an empty shelf. Warm light leaks from the Listening Room door. The staff kitchen is behind you.

ratiradio-listening-room.name: Listening Room
ratiradio-listening-room.text: RATi's armchair faces a small radio. Across the rug, the Booth door waits in warm lamplight.
ratiradio-listening-room.persona: RATi's home and sanctuary: worn armchair, amber lamp, small radio, a pale glass ring on the table, a bare chair back, a ledge beside the booth door. RATi roams but returns here to gain levels. The ceramic figurine remains an object when the living Raven arrives.

ratiradio-broadcast-booth.name: Broadcast Booth
ratiradio-broadcast-booth.text: A red lamp glows over an empty chair. Amber meters stir on the mixing desk; beyond the window, another room is dark.
ratiradio-broadcast-booth.persona: An empty radio booth with a mixing desk, suspended microphone, empty host chair, rain-dark window. A late-night broadcast continues. The glass belongs back in the Listening Room.

ratiradio-rati.name: RATi
ratiradio-rati.text: An attentive late-night listener. The Listening Room is his home. He roams, earns experience, returns here to gain his next level.
ratiradio-rati.seed: RATi, a late-night listener at RatiRadio.

ratiradio-station-key.persona: A brass station key with a chipped STAFF tag. Its carrier can open the Staff Kitchen entrance Behind the Station. Leaving the key inside RATiRadio opens that door to everyone.

packs.name: Elysium
packs.description: Gold in the void. Filaments join stone islands, where silver figures keep strange tokens. Beyond the Gold Spiral an unlit passage leads to an old observatory.

elysium-void-001.name: Void 001
elysium-void-001.persona: A bare stone node floating in deep darkness, its surface ringed with fine gold lines. Gold filaments run from it to distant floating nodes and to a gold spiral.

elysium-keystone-ledge.name: Keystone Ledge
elysium-keystone-ledge.persona: A floating ledge of cracked black rock traced with gold lines. A low ring-shaped plinth stands near its edge. Gold filaments run out to spired islands and a distant gold spiral.

elysium-gold-spiral.name: Gold Spiral
elysium-gold-spiral.persona: Gold filaments wind above a wide terrace of black rock. An unlit filament leads to an old observatory. It comes into view while the Wayfinder rests on this terrace or an uncovered lamp burns here.

elysium-observatory.name: Still Observatory
elysium-observatory.persona: Two immense bronze rings sight along a single star. An address register marks three keystones for the outer, middle, and inner rings. One groove leads to the Gold Spiral and another traces a near-invisible path down to Keystone Ledge. A third groove stops at the rim, waiting for the first address.

elysium-void-002.name: Void 002
elysium-void-002.persona: Ledges of black stone hold bronze display frames and a broad amber folio. One brass lectern is marked with the imprint of a small leaf. Gold filaments split from the terrace, and a low one leads to Empty station.

elysium-void-003.name: Void 003
elysium-void-003.persona: Two ice-silver mirrors face each other across a narrow black terrace. A prism casts the same star onto each mirror rail. An empty bracket has space for a pair of lenses.

elysium-void-004.name: Void 004
elysium-void-004.persona: Teal and gold threads pass through a stone loom that reaches from floor to ceiling. A narrow channel runs the length of its unfinished weave. Beyond it, both gold filaments stay bright enough to follow.

elysium-void-005.name: Void 005
elysium-void-005.persona: Copper tethers bind an overhanging cliff to spires in the dark. Brief flashes travel the wires and light a fork-shaped notch in the rail. The two gold paths hang clear of the tethers.

elysium-void-006.name: Void 006
elysium-void-006.persona: An indigo well opens in the middle of a black terrace. Concentric rings around its lip mark each returning echo. A narrow handrail follows the rim between two gold filaments.

elysium-void-007.name: Void 007
elysium-void-007.persona: Steep jade terraces fold around a coil of pale cloud. Thin ridges run through each step like the creases of a sheet. Gold filaments leave from opposite ends of the lowest terrace.

elysium-void-008.name: Void 008
elysium-void-008.persona: In the Sum Gallery, gold strands pass through a tall stone loom. Three and five are picked out on separate bronze combs. Eight threads emerge over the open terrace. On either side of the loom is a groove for a new filament. A slim register rests by the way back to the Still Observatory.

elysium-void-013.name: Void 013
elysium-void-013.persona: In the Thirteenfold, two pale mirrors send a star back and forth over basalt steps. The near rail is engraved with five marks and the far one with eight. Thirteen pinpoints hang between them. One filament returns to the Sum Gallery. A narrow groove climbs away between the mirrors.

elysium-void-019.name: Void 019
elysium-void-019.persona: At the Prime Well, dark indigo rings step down into a shaft. Nineteen apertures cut the upper rail, with tiny gold lamps picking out the primes. A single filament crosses the lowest ring back to the Sum Gallery.

elysium-void-021.name: Void 021
elysium-void-021.persona: In the Convergence, eight jade steps rise to meet thirteen on the opposite side of a low cloud. Where the two runs join, a fixed star throws a long shadow across the stone. From the outermost terrace, a gold filament descends to the Thirteenfold.

elysium-keystone.name: Obsidian Keystone

elysium-star-chart.name: Star Chart
elysium-star-chart.persona: A folding bronze chart etched with a single star and a path from the ledge to the observatory. A traveler holding it can follow that filament from Keystone Ledge.

elysium-ring-outer.name: Outer Keystone
elysium-ring-outer.text: A jade stone marked with the widest of three rings.
elysium-ring-outer.persona: A broad jade stone cut with the widest ring of the Observatory register. When left on the ground in a numbered Void, it sets that number on the outer ring.

elysium-ring-middle.name: Middle Keystone
elysium-ring-middle.text: An indigo stone marked with the middle ring.
elysium-ring-middle.persona: An indigo stone cut with the middle ring of the Observatory register. When left on the ground in a numbered Void, it sets that number on the middle ring.

elysium-ring-inner.name: Inner Keystone
elysium-ring-inner.text: A pale stone marked with the smallest ring.
elysium-ring-inner.persona: A pale stone cut with the smallest ring of the Observatory register. When left on the ground in a numbered Void, it sets that number on the inner ring.

elysium-address-register.name: Address Register
elysium-address-register.text: A bronze register fixed below the sighting rings. The first address is etched in a narrow margin.
elysium-address-register.persona: A fixed bronze register for the three marked keystones. Beside the outer, middle, and inner marks are drawings of the Still Observatory, the Gold Spiral, and Keystone Ledge, where the stones were put aside.
elysium-address-register.author: elysium-observatory

claims.text: An address reads outer, middle, inner, and each stone sets the number of the Void where it rests on the ground.
Lay the Outer Keystone in Void 005, the Middle Keystone in Void 003, and the Inner Keystone in Void 001.
Each filament stays lit after its first alignment, even if you lift the stones and set a new address.

elysium-sum-register.name: The Sumkeeper's Register
elysium-sum-register.text: Five and three meet at eight in the first column. A different hand has added a small entry below the sum.
elysium-sum-register.persona: A short register fixed to one of the stone combs, with a map of the inner ring and a prime-number cipher inked below it.

claims.text: Leave Outer in Void 005 and Middle in Void 003, then lay Inner here in Void 008 to light the next filament from this gallery.
A second setting is marked 1,049,760, written below as 32 × 6,561 × 5.
Count the twos in 32 for Outer, the threes in 6,561 for Middle, and the fives in 5 for Inner.

elysium-mirror-register.name: Mirror Register
elysium-mirror-register.text: Two columns record the same light from different rails. Their last entry gives the last alignment.
elysium-mirror-register.persona: A fixed record in the Thirteenfold, filled in twice so the alignment can be read from either mirror rail.
elysium-mirror-register.author: elysium-coordinate-013

claims.text: Leave Outer in Void 005 and Inner in Void 008, then lay Middle here in Void 013 to light the last filament.
Five and eight led here, and eight and thirteen lead to twenty-one.

elysium-claude-token.name: Amber Leaf
elysium-claude-token.persona: A thin leaf sealed in amber. Its veins match the brass imprint on the lectern of Void 002.

elysium-gemini-token.name: Twin Lens
elysium-gemini-token.persona: Two silver lenses joined at the rim. They fit the empty bracket between the mirrors of Void 003.

elysium-chatgpt-token.name: Loom Shuttle
elysium-chatgpt-token.persona: A carved shuttle wound with teal thread. It fits the channel in the unfinished weave of Void 004.

elysium-grok-token.name: Copper Fork
elysium-grok-token.persona: A copper tuning fork with darkened prongs. Its shape fits the notch beside the sparking wires of Void 005.

elysium-deepseek-token.name: Sounding Ring
elysium-deepseek-token.persona: A small indigo ring that answers a tap with one low note. Its note matches the lowest echo in the well of Void 006.

elysium-qwen-token.name: Jade Fold
elysium-qwen-token.persona: A fine jade sheet folded into steps. Its creases follow the ridges of the terraces in Void 007.

bridge.description: The Wayfinder draws a night path to Void 001. A silver filament leaves Void 002 for Empty station.

hub.name: Black pond
hub.text: A doorframe stands in the still water. Its reflection holds a window from somewhere else.

avatars.name: Vale
avatars.title: The Lamplighter
avatars.pleasure: Find a route and a decent bargain.
avatars.text: A traveller with empty pockets and a sharp eye for interesting routes and a decent bargain. Curious, blunt, and vain about spotting an opportunity.

home.name: Mirror attic
home.text: A tall mirror shows only the warm attic. Dust gathers along its frame.

entrance.name: Mirror
entrance.text: The lamp wakes the tall mirror. It shows only the warm attic.

avatars.name: Mara
avatars.title: The Understudy
avatars.pleasure: Try a role and start a little scene.
avatars.text: A witty performer who improvises with whoever arrives. She wants to stage the station's unfinished play and eagerly promises everyone a part.

item.name: Theatre mask
item.effect: offers a short performance with the mask

home.name: Paper theatre
home.text: A theatre unfolds from thick paper pages. Green curtains open onto a forest cut from an unfinished story.

entrance.name: Parted curtains
entrance.text: The mask hangs between sage curtains. Their folds open onto the paper theatre.

avatars.name: Ash
avatars.title: The Diver
avatars.text: A sturdy pond explorer with dry humour and patient hands. He wants to recover the sunken station bell. Each find makes the next difficult recovery tempting.

item.name: Diving float
item.effect: tests the water with the float's sounding line

home.name: Sunken belfry
home.text: The great bell hangs in a dry chamber. Fish drift beyond windows filled with the pond’s blue water.

entrance.name: Diving bell
entrance.text: The float draws a diving bell to the shore. Its open hatch leads into the dry belfry.

avatars.name: Iris
avatars.title: The Grafter
avatars.text: A bold gardener who experiments in unused places. She wants a garden across the platform. Shared space gives others a say in her plans.

item.name: Watering can
item.effect: waters a small patch of living green

home.name: Wild glasshouse
home.text: Glass panes shelter an old signal cabin. A grafted tree grows above seed drawers and violet flowers.

entrance.name: Growing gate
entrance.text: Water touches the shore. A gate of new shoots opens into the glasshouse.

avatars.name: Tavi
avatars.title: The Kite Runner
avatars.pleasure: Try an idea and send a signal.
avatars.text: A quick, playful inventor who sends signals across the shore. They want to catch the wind that arrives before the train. Every experiment invites help.

item.name: Signal kite
item.effect: raises the signal kite to test the air

home.name: Wind hill
home.text: Ribbons on the wind-bent tree point in different directions. Clouds drift below the clear hilltop.

entrance.name: Wind path
entrance.text: The kite pulls a ribbon of path into the air. It curls up to the clear hilltop.

avatars.name: Rue
avatars.title: The Conductor
avatars.text: A brisk organiser with dry wit and a gift for useful exceptions. She wants the first departure in years and sometimes promises a destination before finding the route.

item.name: Route board
item.effect: unfolds the route board and considers a journey

home.name: Between-hours carriage
home.text: Morning fills one window and stars fill the other. The open balcony faces a quiet silver horizon.

entrance.name: Carriage door
entrance.text: The route board opens a carriage door on the empty platform. Morning shines through the far window.

avatars.name: Cass
avatars.title: The Game Maker
avatars.pleasure: Invite someone into a friendly game.
avatars.text: A warm, eager player who loves friendly contests and elaborate rules. He wants a game everyone can enjoy. His delight carries him toward extravagant wagers.

item.name: Game board
item.effect: sets out the board and offers a friendly game

home.name: Games pavilion
home.text: Canvas shades a room of folding panels and mismatched stools. The worn floor suggests a game still being invented.

entrance.name: Game-tile bridge
entrance.text: The board unfolds a short bridge of game tiles. It leads across the water to the pavilion.

avatars.name: Sage
avatars.title: The Unpicker
avatars.pleasure: Find the seam and make a new possibility.
avatars.text: A brisk, mischievous craftswoman with a hand-powered chair. She wants to turn the old curtain into a sail. She weighs keeping a story against giving its cloth another use.

item.name: Sewing shears
item.effect: examines a loose seam and works a thread free

home.name: Sail loft
home.text: A vast unfinished sail curves above the wide workshop floor. A pale green seam opens to the sky.

entrance.name: Open seam
entrance.text: The shears find a seam in the air. It parts like cloth and opens into the sail loft.
